_schema.about: Source of truth for the Apps page (apps/index.html). Edit this file, then run python3 scripts/build_apps.py. Statuses are only ever set from a real test run.

apps[].name: display name
apps[].icon: built-in inline SVG name ('node', 'python', 'terminal', 'grid') or a path under assets/ (e.g. 'assets/project-icons/atrium.png')
apps[].kind: how it reaches the system, e.g. 'Prebuilt binary', 'Desktop session'
apps[].workflow: list of the concrete steps the test performs, in order
apps[].install: {label, snippet}: a copy-ready way to get it on Omnix
apps[].verification: null until a maintainer or agent runs the test; then {status, verified_at (YYYY-MM-DD), commit (tested repo commit), notes, log_excerpt}
apps[].known_gaps: optional list of documented gaps from the test file (shown on the card; not a status)
apps[].screenshot: optional path under assets/: a screenshot taken by the app's own test run (never a vendor's marketing image)
apps[].distribution: optional, same shape as on candidates
apps[].section: required: id of an entry in sections[]; the app is listed under that section

_schema.sections[]: ordered list of page sections: {id (kebab-case), title, blurb (one line)}. Every app and candidate names one in 'section'; an unknown id fails the build, and a section with no apps or candidates is not rendered.
_schema.candidates[]: apps not tested yet: {id, name, icon, category, description, section}. Always rendered as untested.
_schema.statuses: passing | patched | known-gap | failing | untested. patched means it works on Omnix because Omnix carries a fix of its own (cite it in notes). passing, patched, known-gap and failing require test.path and verification.verified_at, or the build fails.
_schema.distribution: optional on apps and candidates: {via: 'GitHub releases' | 'nixpkgs' | ..., repo: 'owner/name', release: tag, artifact: file name, url: download or project URL, license: SPDX id, checksums: checksum file name or null, attestation: 'none' | 'verified' (from GitHub's attestations API for the artifact's digest), checked_at: YYYY-MM-DD}. Never mark attestation 'verified' without the API or `gh attestation verify` confirming it.

sections.title: Media and creative
sections.blurb: Video editing, recording and streaming, photo editing and raw development, illustration and visual effects.

sections.title: Documents and publishing
sections.blurb: PDF editing and page layout for print and screen.

sections.title: Developer tools
sections.blurb: Runtimes and the terminal, straight from upstream.

sections.title: Desktops
sections.blurb: The desktop sessions Omnix ships, each booted to a real session.

verification.notes: Fresh NixOS VM run of OBS 33.0.0-beta6 built from omnix-apps/obs-studio master (Omnix-Linux/Omnix#8; the fork now lives in the omnix-apps organization, Omnix-Linux/Omnix#9). The fork carries two Omnix fixes: a guard against a freed core on shutdown (proposed upstream as obsproject/obs-studio#13906), and absolute core module paths on Linux, without which OBS 33 loaded no modules when built by Nix. The test requires every core module to load and a clean exit. The shutdown crash was a race, so a clean exit shows the patched build shuts down correctly; it can't prove the race never occurs.

apps.name: OpenCut 0.3.0
apps.description: Open-source browser video editor (Next.js), built from its v0.3.0 source, served locally and opened in Brave.
workflow: Fetch the OpenCut v0.3.0 source tag from GitHub (no Linux binary, AppImage, flake or nixpkgs package exists); bun dependencies pinned by output hash
Build the Next.js app offline in Nix (next/font's Google Fonts download answered with Next's mock hook and the nixpkgs Inter font)
Start OpenCut's own standalone server on 127.0.0.1:3000 with the upstream .env.example placeholders; /projects returns the app
Open /editor in Brave's official Linux build in an X11 session (--no-sandbox as root, software GL via SwiftShader since the VM has no GPU)
The editor creates a new project and redirects to /editor/<uuid>; the welcome dialog shows
Dismiss it: the editor (assets, preview, properties, timeline) shows "Untitled Project"; take a screenshot

install.label: Build and run from source
install.snippet:
git clone --branch v0.3.0 https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut && cd OpenCut
bun install && cp apps/web/.env.example apps/web/.env.local
cd apps/web && bun run build && bun run start   # then open http://localhost:3000

distribution.artifact: source tag v0.3.0 (f4bd689); the release has no binary assets

verification.notes: Fresh NixOS VM run (nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.app-opencut) on the Omnix base with its desktop preset; the screenshot above is from this run. OpenCut publishes only the web app's source (its v0.3.0 release has no assets; nixpkgs has no package; no flake), so the test builds it from source. The editor's renderer needs WebGL2 or WebGPU: in the GPU-less VM Brave needs --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader, without which it shows "Failed to load project". The editor gates viewports under 1024 px, so the VM screen is 1280x800. Icon: OpenCut's own logo (apps/web/public/logos/opencut/icon.svg, MIT). Test in Omnix main (Omnix-Linux/Omnix#6).
